title: Sleeping Beauty.
lines: Long ago there lived a king and a queen.
They really wanted a child.
And at last, on a lovely spring day, a little princess was born.
She was so sweet and so small.
The king and queen were so happy that they gave a big party.
They invited everyone.
The fairies of the land too.
There were twelve good fairies.
Each fairy gave the little princess a wish.
You will be very kind, said the first fairy.
You will sing beautifully, said the second.
You will be clever.
You will be brave.
And so on.
But there was also a thirteenth fairy.
She had not been invited.
Because the king only had twelve golden plates.
The thirteenth fairy was very angry.
She came to the party anyway, in a black cloak.
She shouted: When the princess is fifteen, she will prick herself on a spinning wheel.
And then she will die!
Everyone was shocked.
The queen began to cry.
But the twelfth fairy hadn't given her wish yet.
I can't take the curse away, she said.
But I can make it gentler.
The princess won't die.
She will fall into a deep sleep.
For a hundred years.
The king had all the spinning wheels in the land burned.
That way the princess could never prick herself.
The princess grew up.
She was kind and clever and brave, and she sang beautifully.
On the day she turned fifteen, she was walking through the castle.
She came to an old tower where she had never been before.
She climbed the spiral staircase.
At the top there was a little door.
She pushed it open.
There sat a little old woman.
She was spinning at a spinning wheel.
What's that?
asked the princess.
She had never seen a spinning wheel before.
Come and look, said the old woman.
The princess touched the spinning wheel.
Ouch!
She pricked her finger.
And straight away she fell into a deep sleep.
And not only the princess.
Everyone in the castle fell asleep.
The king and queen on their thrones.
The cook in the kitchen.
The horses in the stable.
The dogs in the courtyard.
Even the flies on the wall.
The fire in the fireplace went out.
Everything was quiet.
Around the castle a hedge began to grow.
A hedge of roses, with sharp thorns.
Every year it got higher and thicker.
Until you couldn't see the castle anymore.
Only the flag on the highest tower.
People told the story of the sleeping princess.
They called her Briar Rose.
Lots of princes tried to get through the hedge.
But the thorns were too sharp.
Nobody got through.
After a hundred years a young prince came to the land.
He heard the story.
I want to see Briar Rose, he said.
Everyone said: You'll never manage it.
But the prince went anyway.
And do you know what?
That very day the hundred years were over.
The thorns turned into beautiful flowers.
The hedge opened by itself, like a gate.
The prince walked into the castle.
He saw the sleeping horses, the sleeping dogs and the sleeping cook.
He climbed the tower.
There lay Briar Rose.
She was sleeping so peacefully.
The prince gave her a little kiss on the cheek.
And Briar Rose opened her eyes.
She smiled.
Are you here at last?
she said.
And the whole castle woke up.
The king and queen stretched.
The dogs barked.
The horses neighed.
The fire in the fireplace began to burn again.
The cook went on baking his cake.
There was a big party.
And this time all the fairies were invited.
All thirteen of them.
Because now the king had thirteen golden plates.
The end.
